title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-aiden-cho
content:
PR: Improve KV cache eviction + batching heuristics (WIP)
Goal: reduce tail latency for short requests while preserving batching efficiency for long-running chat flows. Notes below are my scratchpad for review and follow-ups.

High-level concerns
- Correctness: ensure no regression of cache hits for resumed chat sessions (prefix KV). Edge cases around prompt truncation and role tokens.
- Performance: microbench shows ~8-12% p99 improvement on short seq lengths but p50 sometimes regresses when batcher waits too long. Need clearer SLO tradeoff.
- Complexity: code added in cache manager is a bit dense; consider extracting heuristics to a small interface + unit tests.

Files to focus on
- pkg/kv_cache/cache_manager.go: heuristics + eviction policy changes. Big function: evaluateEvictionWindow() — large switch, ~120LOC.
- pkg/serving/batcher.go: interaction with cache signals. New signal 'prefer_immediate' added, ensure concurrency safety.
- internal/bench/kv_bench_test.go: perf harness — uses mocked device; results in PR comment.

Review checklist (quick)
- [ ] Thread-safety: check all uses of cacheManager.preferImmediate; is it an atomic bool or protected by mutex? If atomic store/load used, ensure memory ordering between goroutines (Store/Load on atomic.Value or sync/atomic).
- [ ] Unit tests: add deterministic unit tests for short-session cache hit behavior and eviction when sequence length increases. Edge-case: partial KV present (prefix but missing last chunk).
- [ ] Integration test: a simulated chat session that alternates short/long messages to validate hit/miss ratio. Include assertion on average latency < X ms for short messages.
- [ ] Benchmark: add an explicit benchmark comparing old vs new heuristics with seq lengths [32, 128, 512] and batch sizes [1,4,16]. Attach to CI perf job.
- [ ] Lint: go vet/errcheck for goroutine leaks in batcher changes.
- [ ] Docs: add brief note to docs/architecture/caching.md explaining new eviction knobs and how they impact latency vs throughput.

Design/behavior questions for author (Ravi)
- Q1: What are the intended defaults for prefer_immediate? Looks like enabled for user-tier=free by default; is that desired? Should be per-route config, not global.
- Q2: The eviction window uses token-count thresholds + LRU. Any reason not to use time-based TTL for older prefixes? TTL would simplify some cases where long idle conversations keep KV forever.
- Q3: Batcher interaction: when prefer_immediate triggers, do we cancel existing batch windows or only bypass new inflight batches? Potential spike of tiny single-item batches if configured aggressively.

Refactor ideas (low effort -> high)
- Small: extract evaluateEvictionWindow() into evict/heuristics.go with clear inputs/outputs (pure function). Easier to unit test.
- Medium: introduce CachePolicy struct typed config (MaxTokens, MinBatchWaitMs, PreferImmediateThreshold) and thread it via dependency injection. Default policy loaded from config file.
- Large: split cache manager responsibilities: 1) metadata store (indexing LRU), 2) eviction policy (pure), 3) signaler to batcher. Each piece separately testable.

Follow-ups / action items
- Aiden: add unit tests for evaluateEvictionWindow edge cases (deadline: 2026-02-18).
- Ravi: respond to Q1/Q3 in PR thread, clarify per-route config plan (deadline: 2026-02-17).
- Olivia: run full perf job with CI harness + real-device tests and post flamegraphs (deadline: 2026-02-20).
- Team: schedule quick sync (15m) if we want to change default config across clusters — do we need a rollout plan?

Quick perf notes observed on bench harness (local)
- Baseline (master): seq=32, batch=4 => p50=18ms, p95=82ms, p99=240ms
- This branch: seq=32, batch=4 => p50=20ms, p95=68ms, p99=210ms
- Comment: p50 regressed slightly (waiting for batch), p99 improved due to smarter eviction reducing KV misses. p99 win is what we want but p50 impact may affect very latency-sensitive routes.

Testing heuristics to run in CI matrix
- Route profile: latency-sensitive (max wait 2ms), throughput (max wait 10ms), balanced (max wait 6ms).
- Sequence lengths: [16,32,128,512]
- Load patterns: steady stream vs bursty (10x spikes)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cache hit rate, batch size distribution

Open todos in PR comments (copying from author)
- TODO: handle zero-length prefix tokens (edge case in resume flow) — currently panics on index-1.
- TODO: add metrics: cache_evictions_total, cache_hits_total, batcher_wait_time_seconds histogram.
- TODO: document config knobs with recommended defaults per deployment tier.

Notes to self (voice)
- Watch for behavioral change when quantized models (int8) return slightly different tokenization lengths — could shift thresholds. Add small fuzz test.
- Check console dashboards: per-route p99 increased last week for route /chat-stream-latency; might be related to opt-in experiment RB-2026.

Potential rollback plan (if needed)
- Quick revert of config: set PreferImmediate=false cluster-wide via config service (no code rollback).
- If code has bug: revert PR and create a hotfix branch for correctness.

Misc scribbles
- Consider combining LRU score with last-access-time * decay factor to age out long-dormant but frequently accessed prefixes.
- Maybe add a small capacity token for 'pinned' sessions (enterprise customers) so their KV not evicted.

End of scratchpad. Save tests first before major refactor.
